On load, the app asks the server who is signed in through `react-query-auth`, configured in `apps/react-vite/src/lib/auth.tsx`. The `getUser` function calls `GET /auth/me` through the shared Axios instance, and `configureAuth` turns it into the `useUser` hook. `AuthLoader` is rendered in `src/app/provider.tsx` around the whole app, so it shows a spinner until that first request settles. `ProtectedRoute`, also in `auth.tsx`, wraps the `/app` route tree in `src/app/router.tsx`. If `user.data` is empty, it sends the visitor to `/auth/login` with the current path as `redirectTo`. Public screens like the landing page and the auth layout read the same `useUser` hook. `AuthLayout` (`src/components/layouts/auth-layout.tsx`) sends a signed-in user on to `redirectTo` or the dashboard.

Every request goes through the shared Axios instance in `src/lib/api-client.ts`, which adds `withCredentials` so the session cookie is sent. Its response interceptor runs first on any error. It shows an error toast with the server's message, then, for a 401, sets `window.location.href` to the login page. The `redirectTo` it passes is `window.location.pathname`, so the user returns to the page they were on. The error is still rejected afterwards, so the calling code also sees it.

Because the interceptor covers every request, a 401 from `/auth/me` on load also triggers the toast and the full-page redirect to sign-in. That happens before `ProtectedRoute` gets to run its own redirect.

There is a bug in the 401 branch. It builds `new URLSearchParams()` empty and then reads `redirectTo` from it, so the value is always `null` and the fallback `window.location.pathname` is always used. Any query string on the page is therefore lost on the way back. The fix is to read `window.location.search`, which I did not change since you asked for no edits.
